chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazie, and others, they raised it (to the Imam), saying:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Accursed is the one who is a leader! Accursed is the one who intends with it! Accursed is the one who discusses to himself with it!'

key_terms.تَرَأَّسَ: To be a leader / To assume the headship
key_terms.حَدَّثَ: To converse / To talk to oneself
key_terms.هَمَّ: To intend / To have in mind

ai.seo_question: Who is considered cursed in relation to leadership according to this hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (as) establishes a hierarchy of culpability regarding the pursuit of authority, extending the curse from the active seeker to the mere intender and even the internal self-converser, reflecting the Shia emphasis on sincerity (ikhlas) versus ambition. This hadith is central to the doctrine of Imamate, distinguishing between divine appointment (nass) and human striving (tara'us), and serves as a critique of political opportunism in early Islamic history. The progression from action to intention to internal thought underscores that the spiritual disease of leadership-seeking begins in the heart before manifesting in public office.
